Title: From Cassette Tapes to Global Stage: Josphat's Journalistic Journey
NewsSummary: A seasoned journalist's inquiry into the academic world of strategic communications

content.text: In the bustling world of reportorial journalism, Josphat Kioko stands out as a seasoned Kenyan media professional with a unique and inspiring journey. His love for the spoken word began early, in the innocent days of primary school when he would record himself on cassette tapes, eager to share his messages with the world.

His journey into the world of media began in earnest at Shimo La Tewa High School, where he declared his ambition to work for Kenya Broadcasting Corporation (KBC). Despite facing financial hurdles that initially prevented him from attending Moi University for his tertiary certification, Josphat's determination and passion for communication led him to pursue his dreams. His first steps into the world of media came through courses at Lwanga Communication Centre and a job at Baraka FM. Eventually, Josphat's perseverance paid off, and he was accepted into Moi University, where he earned a bachelor's degree in communications and PR.

Throughout his career, Josphat has achieved remarkable success, earning a total of 10 journalism awards both locally and internationally. His dedication and talent have also earned him numerous nominations from the Media Council of Kenya, solidifying his reputation as a respected figure in the industry.

When Josphat came across AKU's advertisement for the master's programme in Strategic Communications, he knew instantly that it was the perfect fit for his career track. The opportunity to learn from world-class faculty, engage in hands-on research, and connect with inspiring alumni like journalists Jamila Mohamed and Peter Mwangi was too enticing to pass up.

At AKU, Josphat is eager to delve into courses on media management and crisis communications management, hoping to contribute to the perpetual evolution of the media landscape in Kenya, Africa and the world. He believes that the media dynamics in the African journalism ecosystem need to adapt to the changing world, and that he is playing a significant role in driving this much needed change.

For those aspiring to a career in journalism and communications, Josphat offers valuable advice: "Learn from your mentors, and make sure media is truly your passion." His own journey is a testament to the power of perseverance, dedication, and a genuine love for the craft.
